gaps.sentence: ___ she was utterly exhausted, she stayed to help clear up.
gaps.explanation: 'Even though' concedes a known fact: she was exhausted and still stayed.

gaps.sentence: ___ fast you run, the train won't wait for you.
The essay was submitted late and, ___, it ignored the brief entirely.
gaps.explanation: 'What is more' adds a further, stronger point to an already negative picture.

gaps.sentence: Far from resenting the changes, the staff welcomed them; ___, productivity rose.
gaps.explanation: Rising productivity is an additional point in the same direction: moreover.

gaps.sentence: ___ the price, the location is absolutely perfect.
gaps.explanation: 'Apart from the price' = the only negative in an otherwise positive description.

gaps.sentence: City rents are crippling. In the countryside, ___, property is far cheaper.
gaps.explanation: 'On the other hand' moves to a contrasting (not opposite) situation.

gaps.sentence: ___ it rains all weekend, the ceremony will still be held outdoors.
gaps.explanation: 'Even if' concedes a possible (not yet real) condition.

gaps.sentence: The plane was delayed; ___, we missed the connection.
